chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Laythi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) who said:

Test our followers at three [things]: at the times of prayer, how well they maintain it; at their secrets, how well they preserve them from our enemy; and with their wealth, how they assist their brethren with it.
ai.seo_question: What are the three tests for Shia followers according to Ja'far ibn Muhammad?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a comprehensive framework for evaluating the authenticity of the Shia community by examining their ritual, social, and financial integrity. This triad highlights that true adherence involves not only private devotion (salah) and communal trust (asrar) but also active economic solidarity (mawasah) with peers, reflecting the holistic nature of Shia identity. The emphasis on 'sharing wealth' underscores the practical application of zakat and khums in strengthening the community's cohesion against external pressures.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-62 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Harun leftover ibn Muslim, on the authority of Al-Laysee that Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“Our followers will be tested under three circumstances. They will be tested as how well they guard their prayers. They will be tested as how well they keep our secrets from our enemies. And they will be tested as how they use their wealth to help their brethren.”
